newsitem.title: USA: Top officials leave minority-owned investment firm.
newsitem.headline: Top officials leave minority-owned investment firm.

text.p: Top officials at one of the nation's largest minority-owned investment banking firms resigned Tuesday in a management shake-up that clouded the future of the pioneering firm.

San Francisco-based Grigsby Brandford & Co. Inc. had no comment Tuesday after senior officials Napoleon Brandford and Suzanne Shank joined New York-based Muriel Siebert & Co. Inc. to form a new municipal finance operation.
The departure of Brandford and Shank followed the resignation Sept. 17 of Calvin Grigsby, founder and then-chairman of the investment banking firm.
After Grigsby left, shareholders of the private firm appointed Brandford as chairman of the board of directors and Shank as president and chief executive officer.
Grigsby resigned shortly after it was disclosed authorities were investigating bond deals the firm handled in Dade County, Fla. Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.
In 1981, Grigsby founded the San Francisco-based municipal bond firm, which grew to become one of the nation's largest minority-owned investment banking firms.

Brandford had been a partner with Grigsby since 1985. Since Grigsby left in September, Brandford has overseen the continuing operations of the firm. Shank became a partner in 1991 and was running day-to-day activities. The firm has 10 U.S. offices.

The 70-employee investment banking and financial advisory firm underwrites, sells and trades municipal bonds, preferred stock, Treasury notes and other securities. It is the only black-owned investment bank to rank in the top 15 senior managers of tax-exempt financial deals.

It was unclear Tuesday what effect the latest shake-up at Grigsby Brandford would have on its operations in California and elsewhere in the United States. Shank said Tuesday that she was unsure at this point what Grigsby Brandford's fate would be.
"We are not sure as to the status of the firm," she said.
One California municipal finance expert said the loss of Brandford and Shank could prove fatal to the firm. "It could be a mortal blow," he said.
In a statement issued by the firm Sept. 26, Brandford and Shank said they were "in the process of restructuring the firm's partnership interest."
"We are confident that over the next weeks and months Grigsby Brandford & Co. Inc. will continue to demonstrate its solid position and contribution to the municipal marketplace," the statement said.
Muriel Siebert & Co. said in a statement issued in New York that it intended to hire Brandford and Shank to develop and expand its municipal finance business.
Muriel Siebert is a national discount brokerage and investment banking firm with offices in New York, Los Angeles, Boca Raton, Fla., and Naples, Fla.
